patients.summary: Retired construction foreman with hypertension, hyperlipidemia and first-degree AV block who joined in 2019 as a smoker and quit in 2020. Survives a type A aortic dissection with tamponade in 2022, stage IIIB lung adenocarcinoma treated with chemoradiation and durvalumab in 2024-2025, and Streptococcus gallolyticus aortic valve endocarditis in 2025 that uncovers a descending colon cancer, resected. Mobitz I block found by cardiology after his last practice visit.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Mr. Woodward is 61 and moving his care here; his prior office was a long drive and he wanted to be able to text a doctor. Records requested from that office.

PMH: hypertension for about 8 years, high cholesterol for about 6. Told several years ago that his EKG showed a slow conduction (first-degree block); never had symptoms, never saw cardiology. No surgeries. No hospitalizations.
Meds: lisinopril 20 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily, a multivitamin. Takes them every morning with coffee.
Allergies: none known.
FH: father had an MI at 68. Mother had a stroke at 72. An uncle on his father's side had a thoracic aortic aneurysm. No other heart disease he knows of.
SH: retired construction foreman, ran crews for 30-some years. Smokes about a pack a day, started in his early twenties, so roughly 40 pack-years. Has tried to quit twice on his own. Beer on weekends, 2-3 total a week. No other substances.

ROS: no chest pain, palpitations, lightheadedness or fainting. No cough beyond a morning clear-throat. No weight change. Bowels regular.

Exam: well-appearing, weathered hands. BP and other vitals in flowsheet. Pupils and fundi unremarkable. Neck supple, no bruits. Heart regular, normal S1 S2, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abdomen soft, no masses, no pulsatile mass. Pulses 2+ and equal at radials and feet. No edema. Skin no lesions of concern.

ECG today: sinus 74, PR 224, otherwise normal. Matches what he was told.

Assessment / plan
1. Hypertension - at goal on lisinopril 20. CMP today.
2. Hyperlipidemia - atorvastatin 40, lipids today.
3. First-degree AV block - stable, asymptomatic. Nothing to do. Will keep in mind before any rate-slowing drug.
4. Tobacco - long talk. He is not ready to set a date; will think about it over the winter. Offered patch or varenicline when he is.
5. Lung cancer screening - meets criteria. Low-dose CT ordered; explained it is a yearly test and what a finding would mean.
6. Colon cancer screening - never done. Does not want a colonoscopy ("not letting anyone put me under for that"). Took a FIT kit home.
7. Hep C and HIV screening once - today with labs.

Return in 6 months, sooner if needed. Flu shot next visit or with the nurse in October.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Woodward, your bloodwork came back fine. Kidney function, potassium and liver tests are all normal, so the lisinopril and atorvastatin are agreeing with you. Cholesterol is reasonable on the atorvastatin, LDL about 100. Hep C and HIV screens negative, thyroid normal. The CT scan scheduling office will call you. Nice to have you with us.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Indication: annual lung cancer screening, current smoker, 40 pack-years. Technique: low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast. Comparison: none. Findings: No pulmonary nodules. Mild centrilobular emphysema is not seen. Airways patent. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. Heart normal in size; no pericardial effusion. Thoracic aorta normal caliber. Mild coronary artery calcification. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. No suspicious osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening with low-dose CT in 12 months.

documents.title: Lung screening CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your screening CT was clear, no spots on the lungs. We repeat it every year as long as you qualify. It also shows a little calcium in the heart arteries, which is common at your age and smoking history and is part of why the atorvastatin matters. Best thing you can do for both is the cigarettes, whenever you're ready.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine check on his BP and cholesterol and a look at his meds.

Taking lisinopril and atorvastatin without missing doses, plus his multivitamin. Feels good. Nothing new to report. Smoke-free for 18 months now.

He came in with a question: his father had a heart attack at 68 and he is 63, so he wants to know whether adding another pill would cut his own heart attack risk further.

Labs from last week: LDL 98, HDL 45, triglycerides 150. Chemistry normal.

Exam: BP 132/84, HR 78. Comfortable. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Nothing abnormal on exam.

A/P
1. Hyperlipidemia / CV risk. We went through it: the main option on top of atorvastatin is ezetimibe. Adding it to a statin lowers LDL further and trims heart attack risk a little more over several years. The absolute gain for someone like him is small but real, and the pill is well tolerated. Also mentioned that a higher statin dose is the other route. He thought it over and would rather stay on what he's on - "I already take more pills than my father did." Reasonable. Continue atorvastatin 40 alone; we can revisit any time.
2. HTN: 132/84, fine. Continue lisinopril 20.
3. Former smoker, 18 months: keep going. Screening CT ordered for November.
4. Flu and COVID booster with the nurse next month.
5. Colon screening: still not done. Reminded him.

events.reason: Sudden severe tearing chest pain radiating to the back

reports.text: Portable AP chest. The cardiac silhouette is enlarged. Lungs are clear. No pneumothorax. No pleural effusion. Bony thorax intact.
reports.conclusion: Enlarged cardiac silhouette.

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia at 118. Low-voltage QRS complexes in limb and precordial leads. Electrical alternans of the QRS. PR interval prolonged at baseline. No acute ST elevation.
reports.conclusion: Sinus tachycardia, low voltage, electrical alternans.

reports.text: CT angiography of the chest with IV contrast. An intimal flap begins in the ascending aorta just above the sinotubular junction and extends into the proximal arch. High-attenuation pericardial fluid consistent with hemopericardium. The coronary ostia are not involved by the flap. Lungs clear. No pleural effusion.
reports.conclusion: Acute Stanford type A aortic dissection with hemopericardium.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
HPI: 64M with HTN, hyperlipidemia, first-degree AV block, former smoker, brought in by ambulance. About two hours before arrival, while sitting at home after dinner, abrupt severe sharp pain in the chest, tearing quality, going straight through to his back between the shoulder blades. Worst pain of his life. No prior similar episode.

PMH: as above. Meds: lisinopril, atorvastatin, multivitamin. Allergies: NKDA. FH: paternal uncle with thoracic aortic aneurysm. SH: quit smoking 2020.

Exam: diaphoretic, anxious, pale. BP 90/60, HR 118, RR 22, SpO2 94% RA. Neck veins distended to the angle of the jaw. Heart sounds muffled. Systolic pressure falls to 85/55 with inspiration. Lungs clear.

Data: portable CXR enlarged cardiac silhouette. ECG low voltage with electrical alternans. CTA chest: type A dissection with hemopericardium.

MDM / course: obstructive shock from tamponade due to type A dissection. Pericardiocentesis deferred given dissection. Cautious fluids. Cardiac surgery at bedside within 30 minutes; taken directly to the operating room.

Dx: acute type A aortic dissection; cardiac tamponade.
Dispo: OR, then cardiac surgical ICU.

events.reason: Type A aortic dissection with tamponade

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Cardiac Surgery Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
Admitted 11/04/2022, discharged 11/13/2022.

Diagnoses: acute Stanford type A aortic dissection; cardiac tamponade (hemopericardium).

Procedures 11/04/2022 (emergent): subxiphoid pericardial window with drainage of hemopericardium on induction, followed by median sternotomy and replacement of the ascending aorta with a tube graft under cardiopulmonary bypass and hypothermic circulatory arrest. Native aortic valve competent and preserved. Coronary ostia not involved.

Course: Extubated POD 1. Chest tubes out POD 3. Sinus rhythm throughout with known first-degree AV block; no heart block or atrial arrhythmia on telemetry. Transferred to the floor POD 4. Ambulating independently by discharge. Incisions clean.

Pre-discharge echo: normal LV function, no residual pericardial effusion, competent aortic valve.

Discharge medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, multivitamin daily; acetaminophen as needed for incisional pain.
Allergies: NKDA.
Instructions: sternal precautions for 8 weeks - no lifting over 10 lb, no driving for 4 weeks. Strict blood pressure control. Cardiac surgery clinic in 4 weeks; follow-up imaging per surgeon. See PCP within 1-2 weeks.

documents.title: Transitional care call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hospital discharge summary and operative note received yesterday and routed to PCP. Called pt 2 days after discharge. Home, pain controlled with acetaminophen, sleeping in recliner. Incision dry. No fever. Bowels moving. Has all of his usual meds; no new prescriptions. Not driving - a neighbor will bring him. Visit booked 11/22 with PCP.

documents.title: Hospital Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed discharge summary. Type A dissection with tamponade, pericardial window and ascending aortic graft 11/4. Remarkable recovery. Will see next week.

conditions.label: Status post Type A aortic dissection with cardiac tamponade
conditions.note: Pericardial window and ascending aortic graft replacement 11/04/2022

orders.reason: Follow-up after type A dissection repair

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here 9 days after discharge. Summary: on 11/4 he had sudden tearing chest and back pain at home, was in tamponade on arrival, CT showed a type A dissection; had a pericardial window and ascending aortic tube graft that night. Out on 11/13.

Now: sore along the sternum, improving, acetaminophen twice a day. Sleeping in the recliner. Walking the hallway and driveway. No chest pain like before, no shortness of breath at rest, no fever, no palpitations. Appetite back.

Meds: lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, multivitamin, acetaminophen PRN. Reconciled against the discharge list - matches.

Exam: vitals as charted, BP 120s/80. Sternotomy healing well, no drainage or erythema, sternum stable. Subxiphoid site healed. Heart regular, no rub, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. No edema.

A/P
1. S/p type A dissection with tamponade - pericardial window and ascending graft 11/4/22. Doing well. Sternal precautions per surgery. Surgery clinic visit in December. Referral to cardiology for ongoing follow-up after surgery.
2. HTN - surgery wants tight control; today in range on lisinopril. He'll log home readings and send them.
3. Lung screening CT this month - cancelled; he just had a full chest CT and the surgeons will be imaging his chest. We'll revisit timing.
4. Family history: his uncle's aneurysm noted again; he wondered whether he should have known. Reassured.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Cardiac Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Woodward in clinic on 12/09/2022, five weeks after emergency repair of his type A dissection (pericardial window and ascending aortic tube graft, 11/04/2022).

He is walking a mile a day and off all analgesics. No chest pain, dyspnea or fever. BP 126/78, HR 76, sinus. Sternotomy well healed and stable. No rub, no murmur. Lungs clear.

Chest x-ray today: stable postoperative mediastinum, no effusion.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, multivitamin. Allergies: none.

Plan: lift restriction to 10 lb until early January, then gradual return. Driving permitted now. CT angiography of the chest at one year. I have asked general cardiology to see him in January for ongoing follow-up. Please continue strict blood pressure control.

Regards,
Cardiac surgery

reports.text: LV normal in size with normal wall thickness and systolic function, EF 60%. No regional wall motion abnormality. RV normal size and function. Native trileaflet aortic valve opens well, no aortic regurgitation. Mitral valve structurally normal, no regurgitation. Ascending aortic graft seen, no perigraft fluid. No pericardial effusion. Normal diastolic function for age.
reports.conclusion: Normal biventricular function. Normal native aortic valve. Intact ascending aortic graft. No pericardial effusion.

TTE today: normal LV function, normal native aortic valve, intact graft, no effusion.

Impression: excellent recovery after type A dissection repair. Stable first-degree AV block.
Plan: continue current medicines; home BP goal as discussed with surgery. One-year CT angiography with cardiac surgery. Cardiology yearly, sooner for symptoms.

events.reason: One-year surgical follow-up and CT angiography

reports.text: CT angiography of the chest with IV contrast. Comparison 11/04/2022. Postoperative changes of ascending aortic tube graft replacement. Graft intact without leak, pseudoaneurysm or perigraft collection. No residual dissection flap in the arch or descending aorta. Aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta of normal caliber. No pericardial effusion. Lungs clear without nodule or consolidation. No pleural effusion. No lymphadenopathy. Healed sternotomy.
reports.conclusion: Intact ascending aortic graft. No residual dissection. Normal caliber of the remaining thoracic aorta. Clear lungs.

documents.title: Cardiac Surgery One-Year Letter
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Mr. Woodward returned one year after emergency ascending aortic replacement with pericardial window for type A dissection and tamponade. He is fully active without chest or back pain. BP 130/80, HR 74.

CT angiography today shows an intact graft, no residual dissection and a normal-caliber arch and descending aorta. The lungs are clear.

Given a stable result, we will move to imaging every two years; next CT angiography November 2025. Continue blood pressure control. Discharged from routine surgical clinic; cardiology continues to follow.

Regards,
Cardiac surgery

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Indication: annual screening, former smoker, 40 pack-years. Comparison: CT angiography 11/14/2023 and LDCT 11/16/2021. Findings: New solid mass in the right upper lobe measuring 4.2 cm in greatest dimension, with spiculated margins. Enlarged right hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes, including a left paratracheal node. No pleural effusion. Postoperative ascending aortic graft. Heart size normal. No pericardial effusion. Upper abdomen unremarkable on this limited low-dose study.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 4B: 4.2 cm solid right upper lobe mass with right hilar and mediastinal adenopathy including a left paratracheal node, suspicious for malignancy. Recommend PET-CT and tissue sampling.

documents.title: Result call: lung screening CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called him myself with the LDCT result: a 4.2 cm mass in the right upper lung with enlarged lymph nodes, Lung-RADS 4B. Told him plainly this looks like it could be a lung cancer and needs a PET scan and a biopsy. He was quiet, then asked good questions. Wants to come in to talk face to face. Booked Tuesday 8/27. PET-CT order and pulmonology referral will go in then; he agreed I could start the authorization today.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

orders.reason: Lung mass with adenopathy; tissue diagnosis

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in to talk through the CT. Feels completely well - no cough, no blood in sputum, no weight loss, no bone pain, no headaches. Breathing normal on stairs.

Went over the images with him. Explained the likely next steps: a PET scan to see where it is active, then a biopsy, often by bronchoscopy through the windpipe with an ultrasound probe to sample the lymph nodes, which also tells the stage. Then oncology.

He asked whether quitting four years ago was "for nothing." Told him no, and that his heart and aorta are better for it regardless.

Exam: well. Vitals as charted. No supraclavicular or cervical nodes. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No clubbing.

A/P
- Right upper lobe mass with adenopathy, Lung-RADS 4B: PET-CT ordered, pulmonology for EBUS, oncology referral placed in parallel so the consult is waiting.
- Everything else stable.
I'll call when results are back. He has my cell through the practice line.

events.reason: PET-CT, EBUS pathology and oncology consultation

conditions.label: Stage IIIB Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (adenocarcinoma)
conditions.note: Right upper lobe, T2b N3 M0; EGFR, ALK, ROS1 negative

reports.text: Specimens: EBUS-guided transbronchial needle aspirates of station 4L (left paratracheal), station 7 (subcarinal) and station 10R (right hilar) lymph nodes; transbronchial biopsy of the right upper lobe mass. Microscopic: malignant glandular epithelium in all three nodal stations and the lung biopsy. Immunostains: TTF-1 positive, napsin A positive, p40 negative. Molecular testing (next-generation sequencing): no EGFR mutation, no ALK rearrangement, no ROS1 rearrangement.
reports.conclusion: Adenocarcinoma of lung origin involving right upper lobe and lymph node stations 4L, 7 and 10R. EGFR, ALK and ROS1 negative.

documents.title: PET-CT and MRI Brain Reports
documents.author: radiology
documents.body:
PET-CT 09/03/2024: hypermetabolic right upper lobe mass corresponding to the 4.2 cm lesion on recent CT. Hypermetabolic right hilar, subcarinal and left paratracheal lymph nodes. No hypermetabolic disease in the liver, adrenals or skeleton. Impression: findings consistent with primary lung malignancy with ipsilateral hilar, subcarinal and contralateral mediastinal nodal disease; no distant metastasis.

MRI brain with and without gadolinium 09/05/2024: no intracranial metastasis. Normal ventricles. No acute infarct.

documents.title: Thoracic Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Thank you for referring Mr. Woodward, 66, found on screening low-dose CT to have a right upper lobe mass.

He has no symptoms. ECOG 0. History of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, first-degree AV block, and emergency ascending aortic replacement with pericardial window for type A dissection with tamponade in 11/2022. Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2020. NKDA.

Workup: PET-CT shows the right upper lobe primary with right hilar, subcarinal and left paratracheal nodes, no distant disease. MRI brain negative. EBUS: adenocarcinoma at 4L, 7 and 10R. NGS negative for EGFR, ALK and ROS1.

Stage: T2b N3 M0, stage IIIB non-small cell lung cancer, adenocarcinoma. The contralateral node makes this unresectable.

Plan, discussed at length with him: curative-intent concurrent chemoradiation - carboplatin and pemetrexed every 3 weeks for 4 cycles with daily thoracic radiation to 60 Gy in 30 fractions - followed by a year of consolidation durvalumab if there is no progression. Pemetrexed requires folic acid daily starting now and vitamin B12 injections every 9 weeks; I have prescribed the folic acid and we will give the B12 here. Port placement scheduled 9/24. Target start 10/3.

We talked about what curative intent means at this stage. He is clear-eyed and wants to proceed.

Regards,
Thoracic oncology
cc: PCP, radiation oncology, pulmonology

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after his oncology consult. Stage IIIB adenocarcinoma of the right upper lobe, T2b N3 M0, no driver mutations on NGS. Plan from oncology: carboplatin/pemetrexed x4 with 60 Gy radiation starting 10/3, then durvalumab for a year. Port 9/24.

How he's doing: "Numb, then fine, then not fine." Sleeping ok most nights. PHQ-2 is 2 today - low mood some days, still interested in things, no hopelessness. We talked; he'd rather keep busy than see a counselor right now. Open door.

Started folic acid 1 mg daily per oncology last week. B12 injection given at the cancer center.

Still no symptoms from the tumor. Weight stable.

Exam: vitals as charted. No adenopathy. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
- Stage IIIB NSCLC: oncology leading. I'll be the home base for everything else. Folic acid added to his list.
- Vaccines before chemo: high-dose flu, RSV and updated COVID today.
- HTN, HLD stable; labs today as a baseline before treatment.
- Mood: adjustment to the news, monitoring. Recheck at each visit.
- Colon screening: not the moment; parked.

documents.title: Implanted Port Placement
documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body:
Procedure: placement of a right internal jugular single-lumen chest port for chemotherapy, 09/24/2024.
Ultrasound-guided right IJ access; catheter tip at the cavoatrial junction on fluoroscopy. Port pocket in the right upper chest. Moderate sedation. EBL minimal. No complications. Port accessed and flushed; ready for use.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Port
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got the port in yesterday. Sore where they put it but not bad. Is it ok to shower? The paper they gave me got wet in the truck.

documents.title: RE: Port
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Yes - showering is fine after 48 hours; keep the dressing on until the clear film comes off on its own or at your first chemo visit. Call the cancer center if you see spreading redness, drainage, or a fever.

reports.text: PA and lateral. Opacity at the right lung base blunting the costophrenic angle with a meniscus, consistent with pleural effusion. Known right upper lobe mass. Right chest port with tip at the cavoatrial junction. Sternotomy wires intact. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Right lower lobe opacity consistent with pleural effusion.

documents.title: Thoracic Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Mr. Woodward is 66 with stage IIIB lung adenocarcinoma on concurrent chemoradiation, cycle 1 carboplatin/pemetrexed given 10/3, radiation ongoing. Background: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, first-degree AV block, and repair of a type A dissection with tamponade in 2022.

Since cycle 1, three weeks ago, he has become short of breath and has a dry cough. Denies chest pain, fever, or weight loss.

He asked what to expect - his chances, and whether there are better options. He had read about a targeted pill for lung cancer that did better than chemotherapy in a trial. I explained that those drugs work on tumors carrying a specific mutation, and his tumor was tested and does not have one, so that drug would not help him; the chemoradiation and then immunotherapy plan is the best-supported treatment for his stage. We talked about curative intent and the uncertainty that comes with it.

Meds: lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, multivitamin, folic acid 1 mg. B12 given 10/1.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2020. Social alcohol.

Vitals: BP 138/86, HR 92, RR 18, SpO2 94% on room air.
Exam: decreased breath sounds at the right lower lobe, no wheezes or crackles. Rest of the exam unremarkable. Port site clean.

CXR: right lower lobe opacity consistent with pleural effusion.

Procedure today: ultrasound-guided right thoracentesis, 900 mL straw-colored fluid removed, tolerated well; post-procedure film without pneumothorax. Breathing easier afterward.

Pleural fluid cytology (resulted 10/28): negative for malignant cells.

Assessment: right pleural effusion, cytology negative - stage remains IIIB. Continue cycle 2 as scheduled 10/24 with radiation.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Outside Note Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Oncology note and cytology reviewed: right effusion drained 900 mL, cytology negative, stage unchanged. Messaged pt to check in.

documents.title: RE: checking in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Breathing is a lot better since they drained it. Still a tickle cough some nights. Radiation makes me tired by afternoon but I'm managing. 7 more treatments.

documents.title: RE: checking in
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad to hear it. Fatigue near the end of radiation is expected. If the breathing gets worse again, call oncology the same day - fluid can come back. I'll see you in December.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Finished chemoradiation: radiation completed 11/14, fourth carboplatin/pemetrexed cycle on 12/5. Restaging CT in early January, then durvalumab if all goes well.

Feels "wrung out" but improving every week. Breathing close to his usual; occasional dry cough. No fever. Appetite fair, down about 4 kg since September. Mood better than in September - PHQ-2 1.

Meds: lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, multivitamin, folic acid 1 mg.

Exam: vitals as charted. Port site clean. Lungs clear, no crackles. Heart regular. No edema.

Labs today: hemoglobin mildly low, expected after chemo; chemistry fine.

A/P
- Stage IIIB NSCLC, post chemoradiation: restaging per oncology.
- Mild anemia after chemo: recheck in 2-3 months; expect recovery.
- Weight: encouraged protein, small frequent meals.
- HTN: fine on lisinopril.
RTC February.

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast. Comparison PET-CT 09/03/2024 and LDCT 08/20/2024. The right upper lobe mass has decreased in size to 2.6 cm. Right hilar, subcarinal and left paratracheal nodes are smaller. Expected post-radiation change in the right upper lobe and medial right lung. No pleural effusion. No new nodule. Right chest port in place. Postoperative ascending aorta.
reports.conclusion: Partial response of the right upper lobe mass and nodes after chemoradiation. Right effusion resolved. No new disease.

documents.title: Thoracic Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Mr. Woodward completed concurrent chemoradiation for stage IIIB adenocarcinoma: carboplatin/pemetrexed x4 (10/3 to 12/5/2024) and 60 Gy in 30 fractions ending 11/14/2024. Restaging CT 1/6/2025 shows a partial response with no new disease; the right effusion has not recurred.

He feels better each week. Cough minimal. Weight stable since December.

We started consolidation durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks today, planned for 12 months. Folic acid and B12 are no longer needed and have been stopped. We reviewed immune side effects - new cough or breathlessness, diarrhea, rash, marked fatigue - and to call us for any of them. Thyroid and liver tests will be checked with each infusion.

Regards,
Thoracic oncology
cc: PCP

documents.title: Outside Letter Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Partial response after chemoradiation. Durvalumab started 1/9, every 4 weeks for a year. Folic acid off the list; durvalumab added as an oncology-administered medication.

On durvalumab since 1/9, two infusions so far, no side effects he's noticed. Energy coming back. Did some ice fishing. Cough gone. No diarrhea, no rash.

Meds: lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, multivitamin; durvalumab every 4 weeks at the cancer center.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Port site fine. No edema.

Labs today: hemoglobin back in the normal range.

- Effusion: resolved on January CT.
- Anemia after chemo: resolved.
- HTN/HLD: stable.
- Mood: good, PHQ-2 0.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted Saturday asking to be seen. Three weeks of low-grade fevers, mostly evenings, to about 100 F at home, with sweats on and off. Tired out - naps every afternoon. Belt is looser; weight down about 4 kg since February without trying. Also describes a dull ache low in the abdomen and constipation on and off for a few months, which he hadn't mentioned because he blamed the treatment. No blood he has noticed. No cough beyond baseline, no dyspnea, no urinary symptoms, no rash, no joint pain. No dental work. No new medicines. Last durvalumab 4/17.

Hx: stage IIIB lung adenocarcinoma on consolidation durvalumab; type A dissection with tamponade 2022 s/p ascending graft and pericardial window; HTN; HLD; first-degree AV block. Has never had colorectal cancer screening.

Exam: T 37.9 C. Other vitals as charted. Looks tired. Port site: no redness, tenderness or drainage. Mouth: no lesions. Heart: regular, NEW holosystolic murmur, loudest at the apex - not present at any prior exam here. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no mass felt. No splinter hemorrhages, no Janeway lesions or Osler nodes, no conjunctival petechiae. No edema.

Assessment: fever, weight loss and a new murmur in a man with a port and a prosthetic aortic graft - endocarditis until proven otherwise. Also differential includes port infection, immune-related effects of durvalumab, or progression.

Plan
- Two sets of blood cultures from separate peripheral sites before any antibiotic.
- CBC, CMP, ESR, CRP today.
- Holding off on empiric antibiotics while he is stable so cultures are not compromised; strict instructions to go to the ED for rigors, confusion or chest pain.
- Oncology informed by message; next durvalumab on hold pending this workup.
- Will call with cultures; if positive, direct admission for TEE and IV therapy.
- The bowel complaints will need their own workup once we know what this is.

documents.title: Today's labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Raymond, first results are in. Your white count is mildly up at 11.8 and your blood count is lower than February (hemoglobin 11.2). The inflammation markers are clearly raised (ESR 62, CRP 48). That fits an infection. Cultures take 1-3 days. Keep checking your temperature and call me tonight or tomorrow if you feel worse.

documents.title: Critical result: blood cultures
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lab called 09:40: both blood culture sets positive at 48 h, gram-positive cocci in chains. Called Raymond: still febrile last night, otherwise unchanged. Explained this confirms a bloodstream infection and with the new murmur the heart valve is the concern. Arranged direct admission to the hospital medicine service this morning; spoke with the admitting hospitalist, who will get infectious disease, TEE, and cardiology. He is driving in with a neighbor.

medications.sig: 2 g IV every 24 hours via port through 6/10/2025

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Staging CT. Comparison none of the abdomen. Focal circumferential wall thickening of the descending colon corresponding to the colonoscopic mass. No pericolonic lymph node enlargement. Liver without focal lesion. Adrenals, pancreas, spleen and kidneys normal. No ascites. No free air. No osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Descending colon mass without evidence of hepatic or other distant metastasis.

reports.text: Specimen: descending colon mass, cold forceps biopsies. Microscopic: invasive moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma arising in a background of adenomatous mucosa.
reports.conclusion: Descending colon, mass: invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital Medicine Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admitted 04/30/2025 by direct admission from his PCP; discharged 05/09/2025.

Principal diagnosis: infective endocarditis of the native aortic valve, Streptococcus gallolyticus.
Secondary: adenocarcinoma of the descending colon, newly diagnosed. Stage IIIB lung adenocarcinoma on durvalumab (held). S/p ascending aortic graft 2022. HTN. HLD. First-degree AV block.

Course:
Blood cultures from his PCP office (4/28) grew gram-positive cocci in chains in both sets; identified as Streptococcus gallolyticus, penicillin-susceptible. Repeat cultures 5/2 no growth. Infectious disease consulted: IV ceftriaxone 2 g daily, 6 weeks from the first negative culture, through 6/10/2025. His existing port was evaluated and judged uninvolved; used for home infusion.
TEE 5/1: mobile vegetation on the aortic valve. No perivalvular abscess. Mitral valve without vegetation. Ascending aortic graft intact without perigraft collection. LV function normal. Cardiology and cardiac surgery reviewed: medical therapy, no indication for surgery at this time.
Telemetry: sinus rhythm with first-degree AV block; no higher-grade block during the stay.
Because this organism is linked with colon tumors, GI performed colonoscopy 5/6: partially obstructing mass in the descending colon, biopsied; scope could not pass beyond it. Pathology: invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated. Staging CT abdomen/pelvis 5/7: no liver or distant metastasis. Colorectal surgery consulted; plan resection after the antibiotic course. Bowel regimen given; no obstruction during stay.
Durvalumab on hold; oncology aware.
Fevers resolved by day 3.

Discharge medications: ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 24 h via port through 6/10/2025 (home infusion); lisinopril 20 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; multivitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; ID in 4 weeks with weekly CBC/CMP through home infusion; colorectal surgery in June; oncology.

Hospital medicine

documents.title: Infectious Disease Consultation
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Asked to see for streptococcal bacteremia. 67M with stage IIIB lung adenocarcinoma on durvalumab, chest port, ascending aortic graft (2022), three weeks of fevers and weight loss, new apical systolic murmur found by his PCP. Both culture sets drawn at his PCP office on 4/28 growing Streptococcus gallolyticus, penicillin-susceptible. TEE today: mobile vegetation on the aortic valve, no abscess, graft without perigraft collection, mitral valve without vegetation. Port site clean.

Impression: native aortic valve endocarditis due to S. gallolyticus. This organism carries a strong association with colorectal neoplasia; he has never been screened and reports months of lower abdominal discomfort and constipation.

Recommendations: ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 24 hours for 6 weeks from the first negative culture. Repeat blood cultures until clear. GI for colonoscopy this admission. The port does not need removal if cultures clear promptly. Will follow.

documents.title: Transitional care call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Discharge summary received 5/9 and routed. Called pt: home since Friday. No fever. Home infusion nurse visited Saturday, ceftriaxone running daily through the port without problems. Taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, multivitamin. Using the bowel regimen. Visit with PCP 5/14 confirmed.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Five days home. Reviewed discharge summary in full.

Summary of admission: S. gallolyticus bacteremia from aortic valve endocarditis (TEE vegetation, no abscess, graft fine), on ceftriaxone 2 g daily through 6/10 via his port. Colonoscopy found a partially obstructing descending colon adenocarcinoma; no spread on CT. Surgery after antibiotics.

Now: no fevers since the hospital. Energy slowly better. Home infusion nurse comes weekly. Bowels moving with the regimen they gave him; lower belly ache milder. Eating.

He said it straight: "So the colonoscopy I kept refusing would've found it." We talked about it without blame. He is focused on getting through.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Port accessed, dressing clean. Heart regular; the apical systolic murmur is still there but softer than on 4/28. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no distension. No edema.

A/P
1. Aortic valve endocarditis, S. gallolyticus: ceftriaxone through 6/10. Weekly labs via home infusion. ID in June.
2. Descending colon adenocarcinoma: colorectal surgery consult booked June.
3. Stage IIIB NSCLC: durvalumab held; oncology will restart when cleared.
4. Anemia: hemoglobin still mildly low, from infection and the tumor. Recheck after surgery.
5. HTN/HLD: continue lisinopril and atorvastatin.
TCM. RTC after surgery; call any time.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Clinic Letter
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Mr. Woodward completed 6 weeks of IV ceftriaxone 2 g daily for penicillin-susceptible Streptococcus gallolyticus native aortic valve endocarditis on 06/10/2025. No fever since early May. Weekly CBC and chemistry through home infusion stayed stable. No rash, no diarrhea.

Exam: afebrile, BP 128/78. A soft systolic murmur at the apex. Port site clean. No embolic signs.

Surveillance blood cultures drawn today. Antibiotics stopped. Port remains for oncology use and was flushed.

He understands to call for any fever over 100.4 F. Resection of the colon cancer can proceed as planned. No further ID follow-up needed unless fevers recur.

Regards,
Infectious disease

documents.title: Colorectal Surgery Consultation
documents.author: colorectal surgery
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Woodward for a partially obstructing descending colon adenocarcinoma found at colonoscopy during his admission for S. gallolyticus endocarditis. Staging CT showed no distant disease. He has finished IV antibiotics. Bowels moving with daily laxative; no obstructive symptoms.

Background noted: stage IIIB lung adenocarcinoma after chemoradiation, durvalumab on hold; ascending aortic graft 2022; HTN; first-degree AV block. NKDA.

Exam: abdomen soft, nondistended, no palpable mass. Port right chest.

Plan: laparoscopic left hemicolectomy on 07/16/2025. Cleared by cardiology and oncology. Completion colonoscopy of the proximal colon intraoperatively or soon after recovery, since the scope could not pass the mass.

Regards,
Colorectal surgery

reports.text: Specimen: left colon, laparoscopic left hemicolectomy. Tumor: adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, descending colon, invading through the muscularis propria into pericolorectal tissue. Margins: proximal, distal and radial margins negative. Lymph nodes: 0 of 18 involved. No tumor deposits.
reports.conclusion: Adenocarcinoma of descending colon, pT3 N0 (0/18), margins negative. AJCC stage IIA.

documents.title: Colorectal Surgery Discharge Summary
documents.author: colorectal surgery
documents.body:
Admitted 07/16/2025, discharged 07/20/2025.

Procedure 07/16: laparoscopic left hemicolectomy with primary anastomosis. Intraoperative colonoscopy of the proximal colon: no further lesions.

Course: uncomplicated. Diet advanced by day 2, bowel function by day 3. Pain controlled with acetaminophen. Telemetry sinus rhythm, first-degree AV block.

Pathology: pT3 N0 (0/18) moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, margins negative - stage IIA.

Discharge medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, multivitamin, acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: surgery clinic 2 weeks; oncology regarding pathology and resuming durvalumab; PCP.

documents.title: Your surgery pathology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Raymond, I saw the final pathology from your colon surgery: the cancer was fully removed with clear edges, and none of the 18 lymph nodes had cancer in them. That is stage IIA. Oncology will go over whether anything more is needed, but this is a good result. How is the recovery going?

documents.title: RE: Your surgery pathology
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Best news this year. Walking laps around the yard. Sore but ok.

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Mr. Woodward is recovering well from laparoscopic left hemicolectomy on 7/16. Pathology: pT3 N0 (0/18), margins negative, stage IIA descending colon adenocarcinoma. Given no high-risk features, adjuvant chemotherapy is not recommended; we discussed this together and he agrees. Colonoscopy in 1 year, then per guidelines.

For his stage IIIB lung cancer, durvalumab resumed today, 1500 mg every 4 weeks, to finish the planned year, now expected in December. Thyroid and liver tests on today's labs normal.

Regards,
Thoracic oncology
cc: PCP

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seven weeks after his left hemicolectomy (7/16; pT3 N0, stage IIA, no chemo needed). Durvalumab resumed 8/5, to finish in December.

He feels the best he has all year. Eating well, weight back up to 86 kg. Bowels regular now, no laxative needed, the low belly ache is gone. No fevers since May. No chest pain, palpitations, lightheadedness or breathlessness.

Meds: lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, multivitamin; durvalumab q4 wk at the cancer center.

Exam: vitals as charted. Laparoscopic port incisions healed. Heart regular, no murmur heard today. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Port site clean. No edema.

A/P
1. Aortic valve endocarditis - treated, cultures clear, murmur gone. Resolved on the problem list. Antibiotic prophylaxis before dental work discussed - will have the dentist contact us.
2. Colon adenocarcinoma stage IIA, resected - oncology surveillance; colonoscopy July 2026.
3. Stage IIIB NSCLC - on durvalumab through December.
4. HTN, HLD - stable. Labs today.
5. High-dose flu today; COVID update when the fall vaccine is out.
Lots of specialists this year; plan to see him here in early winter, will message results.

documents.title: Your labs from Wednesday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news across the board: blood count is back to normal, kidney and liver tests normal, cholesterol where it has been on the atorvastatin. Nothing to change. Enjoy September.

documents.title: RE: Your labs from Wednesday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Finally some boring news. Thanks.

documents.title: Dizzy spells
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Morning doc. For about 2 weeks I get these dizzy spells, a few seconds, and my heart feels like it skips or flutters. Mostly sitting around in the evening. No chest pain, not short of breath, haven't passed out. Should I worry with my heart history?

documents.title: RE: Dizzy spells
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me right away. With your aorta, valve infection this spring and the known slow conduction on your EKG, I want cardiology to look at this soon rather than at your routine visit. I just called their office - they have you Thursday 11/6 at 9:40 and will do an EKG. If you faint, have chest pain, or the spells get longer or more frequent before then, go to the ED. Don't drive if you feel lightheaded.

documents.title: RE: Dizzy spells
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got the call. Will be there.

events.reason: Intermittent dizziness and palpitations for two weeks

reports.text: Sinus rhythm with an atrial rate in the 70s. The PR interval lengthens progressively over successive beats until a P wave is not followed by a QRS complex; the next conducted beat has a shorter PR, and the sequence repeats. QRS narrow, normal axis. No ST-segment change.
reports.conclusion: Second-degree AV block, Mobitz type I (Wenckebach).

documents.title: Cardiology Clinic Note
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Woodward, 67, back in clinic at your request for two weeks of intermittent dizziness and palpitations. He has a history of type A aortic dissection with cardiac tamponade (ascending graft and pericardial window, 2022) and, this spring, S. gallolyticus endocarditis of the aortic valve, now treated. He also has stage IIIB lung adenocarcinoma on durvalumab and a resected stage IIA colon cancer. HTN, HLD, longstanding first-degree AV block.

The spells last seconds, often at rest in the evening. He denies chest pain, dyspnea or syncope.

Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, multivitamin; durvalumab every 4 weeks.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2020. Social alcohol.

Exam: BP 130/80, HR 68 and irregular, RR 16. Irregular rhythm; no murmurs, rubs or gallops. Lungs clear. No edema.

ECG: progressive PR prolongation ending in a nonconducted P wave, then a shorter PR and repetition - Mobitz type I second-degree AV block.

Assessment: Mobitz I (Wenckebach) AV block on a background of first-degree block, with dizziness and palpitations. Usually a benign, nodal-level block, but given prior aortic valve endocarditis I want to confirm there is no higher-grade block and no change at the valve.

Plan:
- 14-day ambulatory ECG monitor, applied today.
- Transthoracic echocardiogram.
- Avoid AV-nodal blocking drugs (beta-blockers, non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, digoxin).
- To the ED for syncope.
Will write with results.

Cardiology

reports.text: 14-day ambulatory ECG patch, 11/06-11/20/2025. Predominant rhythm sinus with first-degree AV block, average heart rate 66. Intermittent episodes of Mobitz type I second-degree AV block, predominantly at night. No Mobitz type II block. No complete heart block. No pauses longer than 2.5 seconds. No atrial fibrillation or flutter. Rare isolated premature beats. Patient-triggered events correlated with sinus rhythm or isolated nonconducted beats.
reports.conclusion: Sinus rhythm with first-degree AV block and intermittent, mostly nocturnal Mobitz I. No high-grade block, no atrial fibrillation.

reports.text: LV normal size, normal systolic function, EF 60%. No regional wall motion abnormality. RV normal. Aortic valve trileaflet; no vegetation seen; trace aortic regurgitation. Mitral valve without vegetation. Ascending aortic graft intact, no perigraft collection. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Normal LV function. Aortic valve without vegetation, trace aortic regurgitation. Intact ascending graft.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Follow-up on Mr. Woodward's Mobitz I block.

The 14-day monitor showed sinus rhythm with first-degree AV block and intermittent Mobitz I, mostly overnight, with no Mobitz II, no complete block and no atrial fibrillation. His symptom triggers matched sinus rhythm or occasional single dropped beats. Echo shows normal LV function, no vegetation on the aortic valve, trace aortic regurgitation, and an intact ascending graft.

He tells me the dizziness has settled. BP 128/78, HR 64.

Impression: Mobitz I AV block without high-grade conduction disease; no pacemaker indicated. Continue to avoid AV-nodal blocking drugs. Recheck in 6 months with an ECG, sooner for fainting or worsening spells.

Regards,
Cardiology

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Indication: surveillance one year after left hemicolectomy for stage IIA descending colon adenocarcinoma.
Prep: good. Cecum reached, identified by appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve. Withdrawal time 11 minutes.
Findings: healthy-appearing colo-colonic anastomosis without mass or ulceration. No polyps throughout the remaining colon. Normal rectum on retroflexion.
Impression: normal surveillance colonoscopy; no recurrence.
Recommendation: repeat colonoscopy in 3 years.
Allergies: NKDA.
